---
description: Sign generated files so hand edits fail the next run, and leave manual sections for people to edit.
---

# Signed files

A generated file is regenerated on every run, so a hand edit to it is lost silently, or, with `check`, fails CI without saying why. Set `signed: true` to sign the file instead, so populate-files can tell a stale file from an edited one:

```ts
import { populateFile } from 'populate-files';

await populateFile({
    filePath: './src/version.ts',
    content: "export const version = '1.2.3';\n",
    signed: true,
});
```

```ts
// @generated-signature v1:… Generated file. Do not edit outside of manual sections.
export const version = '1.2.3';
```

The first line holds a [`generated-signature`](/packages/generated-signature/) token: a hash of the rest of the file. It is written with the file's comment syntax, found from its extension (see [supported files](/packages/generated-signature/reference/api#commentstyle-filepath)). Signed content must be a string.

## What a run checks

Before overwriting a signed file that exists, populate-files checks it was written by populate-files and not changed since:

| The existing file | Result |
|-------------------|--------|
| Has a valid signature | Overwritten, keeping its [manual sections](#manual-sections). |
| Was edited outside its manual sections | `PopulateFilesOwnershipError`, reason `'edited'`. |
| Has no signature | `PopulateFilesOwnershipError`, reason `'not-owned'`: it may be a handwritten file. |
| Has a broken signature or section markers | `PopulateFilesOwnershipError`, reason `'malformed'`. |

These fail with or without `check`, so an edit fails locally and in CI instead of being lost. Move the change into the generator, or into a manual section, and regenerate. To discard the edit, pass `force: true` (`--force`) once.

`force` is also how to start signing a file that already exists unsigned: the first signed run would otherwise fail with `'not-owned'`.

## Manual sections

Mark a region that people may edit with `manualSection()`. Its content is left out of the signature, and kept when the file is regenerated:

```ts
import { manualSection } from 'generated-signature';
import { populateFile } from 'populate-files';

const filePath = './src/client.ts';

await populateFile({
    filePath,
    content: `export class Client {
    readonly baseUrl = 'https://api.example.com';

${manualSection({ id: 'methods', indent: '    ', filePath, body: '// Add your own methods here' })}
}
`,
    signed: true,
});
```

```ts
// @noErrors
// @generated-signature v1:… Generated file. Do not edit outside of manual sections.
export class Client {
    readonly baseUrl = 'https://api.example.com';

    // @manual-start methods
    // Add your own methods here
    // @manual-end methods
}
```

`body` is the content until someone edits it. Add `generated-signature` as a dependency of the generator to import `manualSection`.

On each run, each section's content is taken from the existing file, matched by `id`, so the generator can change everything around it. A section the generator no longer writes fails the run with reason `'orphaned-section'` if someone wrote anything in it, so their code isn't dropped. Rename it back, move the code, or pass `force` to drop it.

`check` compares the result after merging, so a file whose manual sections were edited is still up to date.

## Your own header

A generator that already writes a header comment can put the token in it, instead of a separate first line. `sign()` fills in a token that is already there:

```ts
import { signatureToken } from 'generated-signature';
import { populateFile } from 'populate-files';

await populateFile({
    filePath: './src/routes.ts',
    content: `// Generated by my-router. ${signatureToken()}\nexport const routes = ['/'];\n`,
    signed: true,
});
```

## Catch edits in the editor

populate-files only notices an edit on its next run. The [ESLint rule](/packages/generated-signature/guides/eslint) reports it as soon as the file is saved:

```js
// eslint.config.js
import generatedSignature from 'generated-signature/eslint';

export default [generatedSignature.configs.recommended];
```

## Files without comments

JSON can't hold a comment, so it can't be signed: `signed: true` on a new `.json` file fails with `GeneratedSignatureCommentStyleError`. Record it in a [manifest](/packages/populate-files/guides/manifest) instead, which keeps its hash in a separate file.
